### 11. Addendum: Locked Implementation Decisions (v1.1)

These decisions supersede any ambiguous wording above. They were agreed via
clarification round on 2026-05-19.

**11.1 Architecture: Crane Diamond + DFPkg**
- Built on the Crane framework (ERC2535 Diamond pattern) using the Facet-Target-Repo
  layout described in `manamesh/lib/crane/AGENTS.md`.
- Each `PokerHandSettler` is a Diamond proxy deployed via Crane's
  `DiamondPackageCallBackFactory` from a `PokerHandSettlerDFPkg`.
- **Replaces** `manamesh/contracts/src/GameVault.sol` — the legacy `gameId`-centric
  / fold-auth vault is superseded by the PRD's `handId`-centric design.
- Upgrade path: facet swaps via `DiamondCutFacet` (no UUPS proxy). The original
  §8 line "Upgradable via UUPS proxy recommended" is overridden.

**11.2 One settler instance per ERC20 token**
- `HandInit.vault` = the settler instance address (each settler is bound to a
  single ERC20 token, immutable, set at deploy via `PkgArgs.token`).
- `deposit(amount)` and `withdraw(amount)` drop the `token` parameter from the
  original §6 signatures — token is implicit per instance.
- All players in a hand must transact against the same settler instance
  (enforced by signing over the settler/vault address inside `HandInit`).

**11.3 POC v1 scope**
The following are all in v1:
- `deposit` / `withdraw` (per-token, internal balance ledger).
- `assertHandMembership` (unanimous off-chain sig + per-player on-chain assertion).
- `settleHand` (normal, full-signature settlement).
- `forceTimeoutSettlement` (partial-signature settlement after timeout).
- Rake: `bps` configured at deployment, sent to an immutable operator address
  (both set in `PkgArgs`).
- Level-1 on-chain poker hand verifier (stub — see §11.7 for exact scope).

**11.4 Player cap**
- Contract enforces `2 ≤ players.length ≤ 9` per PRD §2 / §3 (overrides the
  current off-chain module's 2–6 limit; off-chain may stay tighter).

**11.5 Timeout clock**
- The per-hand timeout window resets on **any on-chain activity for that handId**
  (assertion, settlement attempt, etc.). `forceTimeoutSettlement` becomes valid
  after `lastActivity + timeoutSeconds`.

**11.6 Off-chain TypeScript signing helpers**
- Live inside `packages/frontend/src/game/modules/poker/` alongside the existing
  poker game module (`betting.ts`, `hands.ts`, `crypto.ts`).
- Add new files (e.g. `signing.ts`, `handId.ts`) — do **not** spin up a separate
  workspace package for v1.

**11.7 Toolchain alignment**
- `manamesh/contracts/foundry.toml`: bump to **solc 0.8.30**, **evm prague**,
  **optimizer runs = 1** to match Crane (the existing `^0.8.24` pragmas across
  manamesh contracts are forward-compatible).
- `manamesh/contracts/remappings.txt`: `@crane/=../lib/crane/` (Crane lives at
  `manamesh/lib/crane/`, not `manamesh/contracts/lib/`).

**11.8 Engineering invariants (carried over from PRD)**
- `handId = keccak256(abi.encode(HandInit fields))`. The contract recomputes
  `handId` from the supplied `HandInit` on every entry point and reverts on
  mismatch — callers cannot desync `handId` from `HandInit`.
- `finalStateHash` is treated as an opaque commitment by the contract: stored,
  emitted in events, but **not** decomposed / verified on-chain in v1.
- Players in `HandInit.players[]` are sorted ascending by address; all parallel
  arrays (`buyIns[]`, `playerHandNonces[]`, `finalStacks[]`) use the same order.

**11.9 Open items still under discussion (do not implement yet)**
- Force-timeout signature threshold (which subset of partial sigs is sufficient).
- Rake split on force-timeout (operator only vs. operator + house treasury).
- Level-1 verifier exact scope (rank-only vs. best-5-of-7 evaluation).
- Pending-hand lock granularity for `withdraw` (full block vs. unlocked-balance).
- `PkgArgs` final shape (timeout bounds, configurable bps caps).
- `buildHandResult` refactor strategy (replace vs. wrap with adapter).

---

questions.question: What signatures are required to make forceTimeoutSettlement valid?

options.label: lastRoundState signed by ALL + HandOutcome signed by all named winners (Recommended)
options.description: The latest RoundStateTransition (with full sigs from during gameplay) proves the pot. The proposed winners must sign the HandOutcome — nobody can be paid without their own consent. Non-signers forfeit. Best balance of liveness and safety.

options.label: lastRoundState signed by ALL + HandOutcome majority (>50%) of remaining players
options.description: More liberal — a majority can force any payout split. Winners could be paid without signing, but other players collude could push outcome. Higher griefing risk.

options.label: lastRoundState signed by ALL + at least one player signed HandOutcome
options.description: Maximum liveness. Any honest player can finalize after timeout. But one player could try to claim disputed share of pot.

options.label: lastRoundState signed by ALL — HandOutcome itself doesn't need sigs (just lastRoundState pot is split to last-known stacks)
options.description: Skip on-chain reasoning about winners entirely on force-timeout. Pot returns to last-signed stacks. Loses showdown winners' actual claim but is the simplest fallback.

questions.question: Where do forfeited amounts go in forceTimeoutSettlement?

options.label: 100% to operator address (Recommended)
options.description: Simplest. Operator is the same address that receives rake on normal settlements. Aligns with PRD §1 'all go to vault + rake' — in this design operator IS the vault destination. No new bookkeeping.

options.label: Split: configured rake bps to operator, remainder kept in an on-contract house treasury
options.description: Treasury accumulates in the settler; future facet can govern its distribution (stakers, insurance pool, refunds). More flexibility but more state and policy decisions.

options.label: 100% kept as on-contract treasury (no operator cut on force-timeout)
options.description: Operator only earns rake on normal settlements. Force-timeout 'punishment' funds stay protocol-owned. Discourages operator from triggering false timeouts.

questions.question: What does the v1 Level-1 on-chain poker hand verifier actually check?

options.label: Best 5-of-7 evaluation + winner match (Recommended)
options.description: Given hole cards + 5 community cards revealed in HandOutcome, on-chain code computes each player's best 5-card hand, compares ranks, and reverts if declared winners[] don't match. Strongest stub possible without ZK.

options.label: Rank-only sanity check (no card evaluation)
options.description: Verify the declared hand ranks/kickers are consistent with each other (declared winner has ≥ rank than non-winners). Doesn't actually look at cards. Faster, weaker.

options.label: Pure stub — just an interface + event, no logic (deferred to v2)
options.description: Reserve the function selector and emit verification events for indexing, but trust signatures for v1. Smallest contract, but PRD §2 marks the stub as 'in scope'.

options.label: Library + facet split: write the evaluator as a Crane library, attach to settler via a separate VerifierFacet
options.description: Same logic as 'best 5-of-7' but factored as a swappable facet. Lets v2 swap in a ZK verifier without redeploying the settler. Slightly more upfront, much cleaner upgrade path.

input.new_string:
**11.9 Force-timeout signature threshold**
- `lastRoundState` (latest RoundStateTransition) must carry signatures from
  **all** original players. This is the on-chain proof of the pot at the cutoff;
  it was already signed during normal play.
- `HandOutcome` must carry signatures from **all addresses listed in `winners[]`**.
  No player can be paid without their own signature; non-winners do not need
  to sign.
- Any player or third party can submit `forceTimeoutSettlement` once
  `block.timestamp >= lastActivity + timeoutSeconds`.
- Failure modes:
  - If a proposed winner refuses to sign, their share forfeits to the operator
    (per §11.10).
  - If no `lastRoundState` with full sigs ever existed (e.g. abandonment before
    pre-flop), the buy-ins return to depositors' vault balances minus rake.

**11.10 Force-timeout forfeit destination**
- All forfeited amounts go **100% to the operator address** (the same immutable
  operator that receives rake on normal settlements). No on-contract house
  treasury in v1.
- This honors PRD §1's "no player-to-player splitting" rule and keeps state minimal.

**11.11 Level-1 on-chain hand verifier scope**
- Given `holeCards[2]` per player + `communityCards[5]` revealed in `HandOutcome`,
  the contract computes each player's best 5-of-7 hand on-chain, compares ranks
  (and kickers for ties), and reverts if the declared `winners[]` don't match
  the computed winners.
- Implementation: pure Crane `*Service` library invoked by the settlement facet.
  v1 does **not** split the verifier into a separate facet (see §11.9 open
  items below for the v2 upgrade path).
- Does **not** verify the encryption chain (that revealed cards actually
  decrypt from the committed shuffle). That stays off-chain and is captured
  only via `finalStateHash` opacity (§11.8).
- Does **not** apply to `forceTimeoutSettlement` — force path skips card
  evaluation since cards may never have been revealed.

**11.12 Withdraw lock granularity**
- Each player carries a per-settler `lockedAmount` counter — sum of buy-ins
  across their currently-asserted, unsettled hands.
- `withdraw(amount)` succeeds iff `amount <= balance - lockedAmount`.
- The settler ledger only needs `balance` and `lockedAmount` per player;
  the set of pending handIds per player is **not** required on-chain
  (it can be reconstructed from events for indexers).

**11.13 Still under discussion (do not implement yet)**
- `PkgArgs` final shape: confirmed fields are `{ token, operator, rakeBps }`.
  Open: `minTimeoutSeconds` / `maxTimeoutSeconds` bounds on per-hand timeouts,
  `maxRakeBps` ceiling, whether to allow `0 rakeBps`.
- `buildHandResult` refactor strategy: existing TS shape (`Record<address,number>`)
  doesn't match the PRD's parallel-array `HandOutcome`. Decide replace-in-place
  vs. add an adapter that converts between them.
- v2 hook: should the verifier ship as a separate `IPokerVerifierFacet` from
  day one (with the in-Service implementation just routed through it) so a ZK
  verifier can be cut in without touching the settlement facet?
- Root `manamesh/remappings.txt` has the same broken `@crane/=lib/crane/` line
  as the contracts one; decide whether to fix it or delete it (Foundry only
  reads the contracts-workspace remappings).

options.label: Minimal: { token, operator, rakeBps } only (Recommended)
options.description: Each hand carries its own timeoutSeconds in HandInit; per-instance config is just the token, the rake recipient, and the rake rate. Smallest surface.

options.label: Add bounds: { token, operator, rakeBps, minTimeoutSeconds, maxTimeoutSeconds }
options.description: Settler refuses to activate hands with timeouts outside [min, max]. Useful to prevent griefing via 1-second timeouts or 100-year timeouts. Two extra immutable slots.

options.label: Add bounds + rake cap: { token, operator, rakeBps, maxRakeBps, minTimeoutSeconds, maxTimeoutSeconds }
options.description: Belt and suspenders. maxRakeBps is a hardcoded ceiling that even an upgraded facet cannot exceed. Most defensive but rakeBps is already immutable, so maxRakeBps is largely redundant unless we ever make rakeBps mutable.

questions.question: How should the existing TS buildHandResult / PokerHandResult align with the on-chain HandOutcome?

options.label: Refactor PokerHandResult to match HandOutcome shape (parallel arrays sorted by address) (Recommended)
options.description: Replace the Record<address, number> fields with parallel arrays. One source of truth; the TS type directly maps to the EIP-712 struct. Touches buildHandResult callers in poker/crypto.ts.

options.label: Keep PokerHandResult, add a thin adapter to HandOutcome
options.description: Existing callers untouched. New signing.ts adapter converts to the on-chain shape just before signing. Minimal blast radius; two parallel shapes to maintain.

options.label: Define HandOutcome as the canonical type, deprecate PokerHandResult
options.description: Strongest cleanup. Existing PokerHandResult becomes an alias / removed entirely. Largest diff.

questions.question: Should the Level-1 hand verifier be a separate facet from day one for v2 upgrade hook?

options.label: Yes — separate IPokerVerifierFacet, settlement facet calls it via Diamond (Recommended)
options.description: v2 can swap in a ZK verifier with a single DiamondCut without redeploying settlement. Marginal overhead today; clean upgrade story tomorrow. Matches Crane's facet-per-responsibility convention.

options.label: No — inline as a Service library in v1, refactor to a facet only when v2 lands
options.description: Simpler v1, less Diamond surface to audit. Upgrade to ZK will require a settlement-facet recut. Acceptable since we control deployments.

options.label: Both — ship Service library + thin facet wrapper that just calls it
options.description: Most flexible; production code can call either. Most code to maintain.

**11.13 PkgArgs final shape**
- `PokerHandSettlerDFPkg.PkgArgs = { address token }`.
- Operator address and `rakeBps` are **not** baked into the settler. They are
  resolved at settlement time from a separate **Configuration Oracle** (§11.14).
- Each settler holds an immutable reference to the oracle (set in `PkgInit`,
  same for all settlers deployed from a given DFPkg deployment).

**11.14 Configuration Oracle**
- Standalone contract (or Crane diamond) that exposes, per ERC20 token:
  - `address operator` — recipient of rake and force-timeout forfeits.
  - `uint256 rakeBps` — basis points of pot taken as rake on every settlement.
- Lookup semantics: per-token entry if present, otherwise a global default
  applies (default operator + default `rakeBps`).
- Settler queries the oracle at `settleHand` and `forceTimeoutSettlement` to
  determine the rake recipient and rate **at the moment of settlement**
  (config changes during a pending hand affect that hand's settlement).
- Open sub-questions still under discussion: see §11.15.

**11.15 Off-chain TS data model**
- `PokerHandResult` is refactored to match the on-chain `HandOutcome` exactly
  (parallel arrays sorted by address: `players[]`, `payouts[]`, `finalStacks[]`).
- The `Record<address, number>` form is removed; callers of `buildHandResult`
  update accordingly.

**11.16 Verifier facet decomposition**
- The Level-1 hand verifier ships as a **separate facet** (`IPokerVerifierFacet`)
  from day one, attached to the same settler diamond.
- The settlement facet calls the verifier facet through the diamond's selector
  routing. A v2 ZK verifier can be cut in with a single `DiamondCut`, without
  touching the settlement facet.

**11.17 Repository / toolchain housekeeping**
- Root `manamesh/remappings.txt` mirrored to match `contracts/remappings.txt`
  (Crane line updated). Note: there are **two foundry workspaces** in this repo
  (`manamesh/foundry.toml` and `manamesh/contracts/foundry.toml`); the root one
  contains only the default `Counter.sol` scaffold. Decision deferred on whether
  to delete the root workspace or properly populate `contracts/lib/` via
  `forge install`.

**11.18 Still under discussion (do not implement yet)**
- Configuration Oracle details: storage / governance / interface shape (see
  next clarification round).

questions.question: What form factor should the Configuration Oracle take?

options.label: Crane diamond with its own Facet+Target+Repo (Recommended)
options.description: Built with the same patterns as the settler: ConfigOracleRepo + ConfigOracleFacet + ConfigOracleDFPkg. Upgradable via DiamondCut. Consistent with the rest of the system.

options.label: Standalone non-upgradeable contract
options.description: Simple Solidity contract with mappings. Cheapest to deploy and audit. Re-deploying = updating settlers to point at the new oracle (since settler oracle ref is immutable per §11.14).

options.label: Library + a single owner-controlled contract
options.description: Hybrid: storage in a tiny contract, all logic in a library. Smallest contract but doesn't fit the Crane idiom well.

questions.question: Who is allowed to update Configuration Oracle entries?

options.label: Single owner address (Crane's ERC8023 two-step ownership) (Recommended)
options.description: Owner can set per-token entries and the global default. Two-step transfer prevents accidental ownership loss. Simplest v1; can layer multisig/DAO at the owner address externally.

options.label: Multiple operators via Crane's Operable facet
options.description: Multiple addresses (granted by an owner) can update entries. Useful if a small team manages multiple tokens. Slightly more state.

options.label: Function-level operator: per-token role grants
options.description: Each token has its own list of addresses authorized to update its entry. Most flexible (decentralized per-token), most complex.

options.label: Open / permissionless (anyone can set if a slot is empty, then immutable)
options.description: First-come-first-served per token. Trust-minimized but griefing risk (squatters set bad rake rates). Not recommended.

questions.question: When does the settler snapshot rake config from the oracle?

options.label: At settlement time (live read on settleHand / forceTimeoutSettlement) (Recommended)
options.description: Each settlement reads the current oracle value. Operator/rake changes apply immediately to all pending and future hands. Matches your description in the previous turn.

options.label: At hand activation time (snapshot stored on-chain when last assertHandMembership fires)
options.description: Pending hands keep the config they were activated under. Future hands pick up new config. Predictable for players mid-hand; extra storage per hand.

options.label: Snapshot included in HandInit and signed off-chain by all players
options.description: Players sign over the current oracle values during HandInit; contract verifies the snapshot still matches at activation. Strongest player guarantee, but breaks if config changes between off-chain signing and on-chain assertion.

questions.question: How is the global default rake configured?

options.label: Stored on the oracle as { defaultOperator, defaultRakeBps }, also owner-mutable (Recommended)
options.description: Two extra storage slots in the oracle. Lookup pseudocode: if (perTokenEntry exists) return perTokenEntry; else return default. Simplest mental model.

options.label: Use a sentinel address(0) key in the per-token mapping for the default
options.description: Default is just another entry, keyed at address(0). Saves a slot but is slightly less explicit.

options.label: Default is immutable, only per-token entries are mutable
options.description: Forces a known baseline rake / operator that no governance change can alter. Strong guarantee but inflexible.

- Standalone contract (or Crane diamond) that exposes, per ERC20 token:
  - `address operator` — recipient of rake and force-timeout forfeits.
  - `uint256 rakeBps` — basis points of pot taken as rake on every settlement.

input.new_string:
**11.14 Configuration Oracle**

*Purpose.* Exposes, per ERC20 token, the rake recipient (`operator`) and rake
rate (`rakeBps`) used by all `PokerHandSettler` instances on that chain.

*Form factor.* Built on Crane as its own Diamond: `BettingConfigOracleRepo`
\+ `BettingConfigOracleTarget` + `BettingConfigOracleFacet`, bundled into a
`BettingConfigOracleDFPkg`. Upgradable via `DiamondCut`. (Working name; final
naming is an implementation detail.)

*Governance.* Single owner via Crane's ERC8023 `MultiStepOwnable` (two-step
ownership transfer). The owner is the only address allowed to:
- Set / update per-token entries (`setTokenConfig(token, operator, rakeBps)`).
- Update the global default (`setDefault(defaultOperator, defaultRakeBps)`).
- Transfer ownership.

*Storage shape (conceptual).*
```
struct Entry { address operator; uint256 rakeBps; }
mapping(address => Entry) tokenConfig;
Entry defaultConfig;                  // { defaultOperator, defaultRakeBps }
```

*Lookup semantics.*
```
(operator, rakeBps) = tokenConfig[token].operator != address(0)
                      ? tokenConfig[token]
                      : defaultConfig;
```

*Lookup timing.* The settler performs a **live read** on every `settleHand`
and `forceTimeoutSettlement`. Config changes apply immediately to all pending
and future hands at that settler. Hands do not snapshot config at activation.

*Settler reference.* Each `PokerHandSettler` diamond holds an **immutable**
reference to the oracle diamond (set in `PokerHandSettlerDFPkg.PkgInit`).
Swapping the oracle implementation is done via `DiamondCut` on the oracle
diamond — settlers do not need to change.

*Default config governance.* The global default is itself owner-mutable
(not a hardcoded baseline). v1 ships with `defaultOperator` and
`defaultRakeBps` set at deployment.

*Events.* Oracle emits typed events on each entry/default change for indexers.
(Specific event signatures to be defined during implementation.)

*Out of scope for v1.* No per-table or per-hand rake overrides; no oracle-level
`maxRakeBps` ceiling (owner is trusted); no batch update entry points (single-
entry mutators only — batching is an off-chain script concern).

The `BettingConfigOracle` is a Crane Diamond that exposes per-ERC20-token rake configuration `{operator, rakeBps}` for the poker settler diamonds to query at settlement time. ---
name: manamesh-boardgameio-crypto-package
description: The @manamesh/boardgameio-crypto leaf package — what it owns and how games consume it
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 66d4fbbd-bfc2-424e-af93-b43b71f69cff
---

`packages/boardgameio-crypto/` (`@manamesh/boardgameio-crypto`) is the shared
cryptographic primitives package — formerly `@manamesh/crypto` at `packages/crypto/`,
renamed and consolidated to absorb the (now-deleted) `@cyotee/boardgameio-crypto`
inner submodule that lived at `packages/manamesh/packages/boardgameio-crypto/`.

It is a LEAF package — zero internal deps — so frontend → boardgameio-crypto and
poker → boardgameio-crypto are one-way (no cycles). Owns: mental-poker (SRA),
Merkle commitments, EC ElGamal, Feldman DKG, DLEQ, ECDSA, Paillier HE, Shamir
SSS, snarkjs ZK helpers, the boardgame.io crypto plugin, and setup-flow helpers
under `integration/setup-utils` (absorbed from the deleted submodule — the five
symbols `getCurrentSetupPlayer`, `advanceSetupPlayer`, `resetSetupPlayer`,
`lookupCardIdFromPoint`, `deterministicShuffle`).

- It defines its own minimal `CoreCard` in `plugin/crypto-plugin.ts` (frontend's
  `game/modules/types.ts` keeps its own, structurally compatible — do NOT couple
  the crypto package back to frontend types).
- Consumers import via explicit subpath exports
  (`@manamesh/boardgameio-crypto/mental-poker`, `/plugin/crypto-plugin`, `/merkle`,
  `/paillier`, `/zk`, `/integration/setup-utils`, etc.) to keep heavy snarkjs/paillier
  out of light code-split chunks. Barrel `@manamesh/boardgameio-crypto` also works.
- No `typecheck` script: the code carries pre-existing latent strict-mode type
  debt (frontend ships via esbuild, never ran tsc). Vitest is the gate (124 tests).

Cleanup gotcha when renaming: the deleted inner submodule was referenced as a
TypeScript project reference in `packages/manamesh/tsconfig.json` and
`packages/manamesh/packages/frontend/tsconfig.json`. Vitest (via vite's TS
resolution) crashes parsing the missing tsconfig before the test suite can run.
Always grep tsconfig `references` arrays when removing a workspace package.

Sibling packages: `@manamesh/poker` (`packages/poker/`) and `@manamesh/onepiece`
(`packages/onepiece/`) both consume this. Poker also holds the Solidity
settlement contracts. See [[dual-root-yarn-frontend-tests]] for how to run the
frontend suite.

# @manamesh/boardgameio-crypto

Shared cryptographic primitives for ManaMesh's provably-fair P2P card games.

This is a **leaf package** — it has no dependencies on `@manamesh/frontend` or any
other in-tree package, so it can be consumed freely without import cycles.

## Consumers

- `@manamesh/frontend` — War, Go Fish, OnePiece, Threshold Tally, Battleship game modules.
- `@manamesh/poker` — mental-poker dealing + the EIP-712 settlement flow.
